# `start_planet_stack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Stack a recorded planetary, lunar or solar video file into an image on a worker thread.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe2120, StartPlanetStack @0x333ee0 (64-bit build) |

Copies file, mode and region into the global stack parameters, stops any AVI reading, resolves the input path, checks free disk and starts the PlanetStack worker. The output name is built from the mode and the current date and time with a .fit extension. A success reply establishes only that the worker was launched, not that the input is usable, that the disk was measured, or that an image was produced. Progress and the final state arrive as PlanetStack events; failure also produces a PlanetStack event with state fail and a code and error string.

Side effects: Writes shared stack parameters and status, stops AVI reading, resolves paths, and starts the named PlanetStack worker thread. Does not wait for the final image.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_planet_stack"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Object-only: any other params container yields an empty map and 102. Unknown members are unused. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build): the parser and starter read no direction_true member; the request members remain file, optional mode and optional rect (READ). direction_true is a compass member of get_device_state. [READ] |
| `params.file` | string | yes | - | Input video or image file to stack. Missing, null or non-string gives 102. [READ] |
| `params.mode` | string | no | "" | One of lunar (alias moon), solar (alias sun), planet; exact-match names map to modes 2, 3 and 4. Empty or unrecognized: the device tries a case-insensitive match of those names against the file name and fails with 102 if none is found. A non-string is ignored (treated as empty). [READ] |
| `params.rect` | array<integer> | no | absent; all four values -1 (no region) | Region of interest as four integers [x, y, width, height]; all four required if rect is given, extra elements ignored, no range check. A null or non-array rect gives 102. Integers are signed 32-bit. Range: at least 4 item(s). [READ] |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 102 | file missing or not a string, params not an object, rect present but malformed or null, or mode not given and not detectable from the file name | `invalid params` |
| 268 | The PlanetStack worker thread is running (as read from the handler; exact check unresolved) | `operation is in progress` |
| 524 | A batch stack, View or continuous-exposure function conflicts | `function conflict` |
| 536 | A ViewPlan worker is running | `view plan is already running` |
| 208 | Free-space query succeeded and reported at most 199 binary megabytes | `disk is full` |
| 212 | Worker thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

If the free-disk query itself fails, the disk guard is bypassed and the request can still succeed (64-bit build; not re-derived for the 32-bit build). Other path and delegated failure codes are not exhaustively established. Later input, disk and worker failures are reported through events, not this reply.

## Example

Request, stack-with-mode:

```json
{"id":111,"method":"start_planet_stack","params":{"file":"Video_Example.avi","mode":"planet"}}
```

Request, stack-with-rect:

```json
{"id":112,"method":"start_planet_stack","params":{"file":"Video_Example.avi","mode":"lunar","rect":[100,80,640,480]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_planet_stack","result":0,"code":0,"id":111}
```

Reply, plan-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_planet_stack","error":"view plan is already running","code":536,"id":113}
```
